answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioral Fingerprinting. Each identity accumulates a signed action history; a rotating sonnet-derived nonce seeds challenge tasks, so honest agents re-derive consistent responses across epochs while copies diverge. A willow-shaped similarity graph clusters histories, and any vine of near-identical new identities is flagged and throttled. To pass, an attacker must operate every sybil through many epochs with independent, costly behavior generation — roughly hours of compute and unique interactions per identity.
